facts.text: A pressure-over-liquid instrument pressurises a liquid reservoir with the PGVA and opens a solenoid valve via the VAEM for a calibrated duration; the calibration maps target volume (uL) to valve opening time (ms)
The Dispenser class is the fixed-volume, non-aspirating entry point; the Pipettor class extends it with aspirate, mix and tip-handling operations
Dispense takes a mapping of channel IDs to {volume in uL, liquid_class} commands and applies the pressure-over-liquid process to each selected valve channel
Aspirate takes the same channel-command mapping as dispense and runs the aspirate calibration process
Mix repeats an aspirate and a dispense on the channel for the requested number of cycles
A transfer aspirates a volume and then dispenses it; both operations take the same channel-command mapping but use their own calibrated pressure
The calibration parameter parameters.pressure is the PGVA output pressure in mbar for one liquid class and process
The active valve channel IDs come from active_valve_terminals and the channel count from fluid-channel-count in the component configuration
The liquid classes are the keys of the live calibration mapping
The session returns the active channel IDs, the liquid-class names and the combined fluid-control, pressure and valve status
set_pressure takes a target pressure in mbar, sends it to the pressure controller and blocks until the reading stabilises
An output pressure of 0 mbar is the neutral value the manual valve command uses by default
The component context-manager exit sets the pressure to 0, deselects every valve and clears the fluid-control status
_wait_output_pressure issues set_output_pressure and then polls get_output_pressure until the reading is within 1 mbar of the target
The pressure-readiness and valve-readiness polling loops are bounded by a 30 second timeout
The engine rejects a negative volume, a channel that is not in the active channel configuration and a non-positive valve opening time
The fluid-control status codes are 0 clear, 1 error and 2 busy
The upstream pressure validator is a no-op TODO, so the library itself does not enforce a pressure range
